title: Giant Bicycle Recalls LED-Light Keys Included with SureLock Bike Lock Sets Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion; Violates Mandatory Standard for Consumer Products with Button Cell Batteries
hazard: The LED-light key that was included with certain SureLock Bicycle Lock sets violates the mandatory safety standard for consumer products with button cell and coin batteries because the button batteries can be accessed easily by children, posing an ingestion hazard. Additionally, the packaging and product do not have the warnings required under Reese’s Law. When button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, internal chemical burns, and death.
description: This recall involves Giant Bicycle-branded black-and-white LED-light bike lock keys that were included as part of a pre-keyed SureLock bicycle lock set that includes a bike lock and two-or-four keys without an LED-light (depending on the model). Only LED-light bike lock keys manufactured after March 2023 are included in this recall. The list of affected serial numbers is included in the table below. Serial numbers are located on the underside of the bike lock, as shown in the below picture.
remedy:
Consumers should stop using the recalled LED-light key that was included with certain SureLock Bicycle Lock sets immediately and contact Giant Bicycle for a $5 refund. Consumers will be asked to bring the LED key to an authorized Giant retailer to participate in the recall and receive the refund. When returning the LED-light key to a retailer, consumers will be required to bring either the complete bicycle lock purchase or a picture of the serial number on the bicycle lock in order to verify the serial number is in the scope of the recall. Consumers may continue to use the bicycle lock and non-LED-light keys included with the SureLock Bicycle Lock sets.  


Note: Button and Coin cell batteries are hazardous. Batteries should be disposed of or recycled by following local hazardous waste procedures.

title: E-One Incorporated: Wire Harness and Busbar May Overheat
hazard: An overheated busbar can increase the risk of a fire.
description: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM E-One Incorporated (E-One) is recalling certain 2024-2026 Typhoon N, 2025-2026 Cyclone N, and 2026 Cyclone II fire trucks. The positive power supply may be loose, causing the wiring harness and busbar to overheat.
remedy: E-ONE will provide a replacement wiring harness and busbar, free of charge.  Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed October 20, 2026. Owners may contact E-One customer service at 1-352-237-1122.

title: Blue Bird Body Company: High Voltage Battery Mounting Bolts May Be Loose or Missing
hazard: A high voltage battery with loose or missing mounting bolts can cause a loss of drive power, increasing the risk of a crash.
description: ELECTRICAL SYSTEM Blue Bird Body Company (Blue Bird) is recalling certain 2018-2024, 2026 Vision and All American Electric school buses. The high voltage battery system mounting bolts may be loose or missing.
remedy: Dealers will inspect and reinstall bolts with thread locker. Damaged or missing bolts will be replaced. All repairs will be performed free of charge. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed December 1, 2026. Owners may contact Blue Bird customer service at 1-478-822-2242. Blue Bird's number for this recall is R26AK.

title: Toys: Transport vehicle truck
hazard: Chemical, Choking. The battery compartment screw does not comply with the requirements for battery compartment fasteners because it becomes detached when loosened. As a result, the button batteries inside are easily accessible. A small child may put the batteries in the mouth and swallow them, which could cause choking and/or severe internal injuries to the gastrointestinal tract. The screw or fastener must remain attached to the battery cover or compartment door when loosened or opened.
description: A plastic toy logging truck consisting of an orange cab and a grey cargo bed loaded with imitation wooden logs. The logs are secured to the vehicle with elastic retaining bands. The product does not comply with the requirements of the Toy Safety Directive nor with European standard EN 62115.

title: Electrical Appliances: DM132
hazard: Electric_Shock. The windings in the transformer are not properly fixed or insulated and are too close to the metal parts. Additionally, the safety distances on the printed circuit board are too small and the distance between the live parts and the appliance’s outer casing is insufficient. As a result, accessible parts could become live, increasing the risk of electric shock.
description: White USB wall charger The product does not comply with the requirements of the Low Voltage Directive.
